text:
david: customer reports streaming response abruptly closed mid-token, they see truncated output and our billing shows a 5xx on the session. customer invoice ID inv_2026_04_22_99. see attached transcript they pasted. can eng/sre confirm whether this should be billed?

maya: can you paste the gateway logs + the original request headers? which model + route?

david: route: POST /v1/generate/stream, model: open-redwood-3-large, content-type: chunked/multipart. curl they used:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"long prompt...","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream
```

raj: pulled gateway logs for that time window (3265554300-3265554400). seeing this pattern:
```
2026-04-22T15:12:05.123Z gateway: write to client failed: write tcp 10.1.2.3:443->10.4.5.6:53421: write: broken pipe
2026-04-22T15:12:05.123Z gateway: upstream status: 200, bytes_sent: 0, error_classified: 5xx
2026-04-22T15:12:05.124Z router: marked request as gateway_error, code=EPIPE
```
looks like gateway saw downstream socket close while trying to flush a chunk and our accounting path increments 5xx counters because upstream didn't finish a normal close.

ben: +1 this smells like the EOF vs upstream failure classification race. If the proxy reports `broken pipe` during write and we haven't sent any final chunk metadata, we currently route to 5xx. We should treat `write: broken pipe` as a candidate client-abort unless upstream explicitly returned an error body/status.

maya: customer says they kept their client open but network flaked for ~200ms and client retried, they assume they shouldn't be billed. We need repro steps to prove classification mismatch.

david: quick repro I used locally: run a simple server that sends chunked responses slowly, then kill the TCP stream from the client side mid-chunk. repro server code (python):
```python
import http.server, socketserver, time
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
  def do_POST(self):
    self.send_response(200)
    self.send_header('Transfer-Encoding','chunked')
    self.end_headers()
    for i in range(10):
      chunk = f"chunk {i}\n".encode()
      self.wfile.write(hex(len(chunk))[2:].encode()+b"\r\n")
      self.wfile.write(chunk+b"\r\n")
      self.wfile.flush()
      time.sleep(0.2)

socketserver.TCPServer(('0.0.0.0',8000), H).serve_forever()
```
then `nc` to connect and `kill -9` the `nc` process while server is mid-send. On our gateway, that produced the broken pipe trace above.

raj: thanks. suggested classification change: if proxy write fails with EPIPE/ECONNRESET and `bytes_sent > 0` and upstream status==200, mark as client-abort (do not increment 5xx billing). If `bytes_sent==0` and no upstream error, still treat as client-abort (client never consumed content). Only increment 5xx when upstream returns explicit 5xx or upstream internal error is logged. Edgecases: partial bytes_sent and last_chunk_seen flags.

ops-bot: alert: gateway:eof_count spike at 2026-04-22T15:12, 80% of spikes @region-us-west.

taylor: billing here — customer will dispute invoice if we don't credit. Can we do a rollback or issue credit pending fix? What's the estimated fix ETA?

ben: low-risk patch: change billing classification in accounting service to prefer upstream_status when available; treat `broken pipe` as client-cancel unless router logged upstream 5xx. I can prepare PR, test in staging today, roll to prod with feature flag. ETA ~ 6 hours to staged PR + 3 hours verification.

maya: actionable list: 1) eng (ben/raj) push classification patch behind flag, 2) SRE (raj) add a metric `gateway.client_abort_vs_5xx` and an alert when false-5xx rate > 1% of total errors, 3) support (david) open credit hold for inv_2026_04_22_99 and customers impacted, 4) ops-bot to mute billing automation for disputed invoices matching this pattern.

david: I put the invoice on hold and emailed the customer acknowledging we're investigating. they asked for repro steps (sent the python snippet). I'll follow up after patch.

raj: I'll add unit tests that simulate socket close during chunk flush, assert accounting increments client_abort counter not 5xx, and add integration test against staging gateway to ensure metrics flow.

taylor: please include CI proof so billing can proceed with credits. Also provide a short support-facing blurb we can use for the customer: `We observed a downstream TCP reset during the streaming response which our system previously classified as a gateway error. We're updating classification to treat this as a client disconnect and will issue a credit. ETA for visibility: ~end of day.`

ben: will open PR and tag @maya @raj @david. putting temporary feature flag `billing.strict_5xx=false` for rollout.

maya: thanks all. once PR lands, schedule a short postmortem with bullet actions and timeline.

david: customer happy to wait for fix + credit; they asked if this could be prevented client-side — suggested best practice: enable client side retry/backoff and check server's half-close behavior. shared a short note to customer.

raj: last note — add log enrichment: include `client_socket_state` and `bytes_last_sent` to make future debugging easier.

ben: PR #4128 opened: https://phabricator.redwood/4128 (feature flag on). staging run green at 3265556800. planning prod deploy 3265561200 unless rollback needed.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: staging -> prod @ 2026-04-22T19:00 UTC (ticket: infra-847).

maya: closing loop: support to confirm invoice credit & follow up with customer, eng/sre monitor metric for 24h.
